name: groundwork
description: Reasoning discipline for AI agents — cross-model audit, a deeper two-round debate audit, cross-CLI routing, a reasoning baseline that builds its own modular FPF corpus from upstream, and an evidence-before-claim verification gate. Five plugins that turn a single AI session into a calibrated one.

plugins.name: tribunal
plugins.description: Independent code review by other AI CLIs. Whichever CLI you are running stays as the arbiter; the others (any combo of Claude, Codex, Gemini, Grok) audit the code in parallel and you read every verdict before deciding. Standard mode runs two auditors; --critical runs all three others. Use for pre-merge reviews, security-critical code, and changes you don't want to ship alone.

plugins.name: conclave
plugins.description: Two-round debate audit — the deep sibling of tribunal. All other CLIs (Claude, Codex, Gemini, Grok) audit independently at max effort, then each re-judges after seeing every round-1 verdict; the arbiter synthesizes all of it. A closing GPT-5.5 historian scores each model and appends the run to a history log so you can track which models audit best over time. For the hardest security/architecture/pre-prod calls where one pass isn't enough.

plugins.name: delegate
plugins.description: Routing matrix for sending work to another AI CLI. Tells you which model and which reasoning effort to use for each task — code review, architecture analysis, whole-project scans, quick documentation, web-aware questions. Uses raw codex exec, gemini, and grok -p binaries; no wrapper required.

plugins.name: fpf
plugins.description: Reasoning baseline plus a local builder for the full FPF corpus. The SKILL.md ships the always-loaded operational subset (ADI cycle, calibration tags, I/D/S, weakest-link). A bundled refresh script pulls the upstream ailev/FPF spec and splits it into navigable modules, cards, and a relation graph on first use — and silently no-ops when upstream hasn't moved. No FPF text is bundled with the plugin.

plugins.name: evidence-gate
plugins.description: Refuses to claim completion without proof. Identifies the command that would prove the claim, runs it fresh, reads the actual output, and reports PASS or FAIL with the evidence. Companion to the tag discipline in fpf — the gate that makes [OBSERVED] tags trustworthy.
